aspects.says: A response with a wrong or missing MAC proves nothing, so the outcome is unknown, as with no answer: reverse and alert, never report a decline.
basis: section:7.6 A Response That Fails Its MAC Is an Unknown Outcome, Not a Decline

aspects.says: Card numbers travel intact and are masked only in logs and displays; track data, CVV and PIN blocks are never kept after the purchase.
basis: section:7.7 Card Data Crosses the Client Intact and Stays Nowhere

aspects.says: A key's bytes differ between modules because each holds it under its own LMK; the check value identifies the key and is compared at every load, import and exchange.
basis: section:7.4.1 Two Modules, One Key, Different Bytes
section:7.4.2 A Key Exchange Is Checked Before It Is Used

aspects.says: A JCESecurityModule with the Bouncy Castle provider, an LMK kept in memory and keys loaded from published test components gives reproducible PIN and MAC results without hardware.
basis: section:7.1 A Security Module on Your Desk
aspects.reason: the desk module and test acquirer are the tool the practices' tests are built on, not a skill to practise

aspects.says: The MAC covers the packed message as sent, with the MAC field's bit set and its own bytes left out, computed on a copy so a received MAC is never overwritten.
basis: section:7.5 A MAC Covers the Bytes as Sent, So It Is the Last Thing You Add

aspects.says: The module is deployed as an SMAdaptor QBean; on Java 17 without a named provider it never registers, while the rest of Q2 runs, and SunJCE lacks the default MAC.
basis: section:7.4 Keys Live Under the Module's Master Key and Are Known by Their Check Value

aspects.says: A format 0 PIN block is the PIN mixed with 12 digits of the card number and encrypted under a PIN key, so reading it takes both the key and the card number.
basis: section:7.2 A PIN Block Means Nothing Without Its Key and Its Card Number

aspects.says: Signing is the last change before a message leaves; any field set after it makes the host reject the message.
basis: section:7.5 A MAC Covers the Bytes as Sent, So It Is the Last Thing You Add

aspects.says: TLS protects one connection and ends in an ordinary process at each end, while a PIN block stays encrypted until it reaches a module that holds its key.
basis: section:7.2 A PIN Block Means Nothing Without Its Key and Its Card Number

aspects.says: The client re-encrypts a PIN block from the terminal's key and format to the host's with translatePIN, and refuses a purchase whose block cannot be translated rather than sending it without field 52.
basis: section:7.3 The Client Translates the PIN and Never Sees It
